craft_notes: Sthāyin: touch-delight (heart-pleasing). Rows: row 3 (touch-blooms→honor). Close: honor (namāmi distinct from praise/bow — three verbs kept distinct across songs). Rejected: 'pleases' for delights — killed: gladdens/delights kept (toṣayati as joy-giving); 'goddess of touch' — killed: skin-formed kept (tvac precise).

lines: Westward firm on her petal, with heart-gladding touch-blooms —
she gladdens Bhairava, skin-formed Vārāhī — honor.
l4.sanskrit_cite: paścimadigdalasaṃsthā hṛdayaharaiḥ sparśakusumairyā | toṣayati bhairavaṃ tāṃ tvagrūpadharāṃ namāmi vārāhīm

reads_against.argmap: Who offers touch? → Vārāhī (tvac/touch, west petal) pleases Bhairava with tactile offerings.
c1_essence: Vārāhī skin-formed delights with touch-flowers from the west: feeling itself pleasing.
reads_against.c1_rasa: adbhuta settling toward śānta (wonder circling home to rest)
